HRA Analysis: ROYAL PRINCESS (1) showed gate speed last time out before being shuffled back a touch and was still able to run on late not beaten far behind So Many Moments. She may elect to lead this time and can run well from there. TAYLORS FOUR (8) secured a good run behind the leader last time out and was running on nicely into third behind So Many Moments. She should get a similar run in this race and can be running on late again. ULTIMATE ARK (7) was a good winner two starts ago when being shuffled back on the pegs early before sprinting nicely to reel in Uncut Gem. He may be shuffled back from a wide draw but does appear to be one of the class runners in this field. OCTOBER RACKETEER (12) has been in excellent form recently having won 3 of her last 5 starts including his latest start when leading and holding off the late challenge of Last Call. He draws poorly and will need a few things to go his way this time. SELECTIONS: ROYAL PRINCESS (1), TAYLORS FOUR (8), ULTIMATE ARK (7), OCTOBER RACKETEER (12) SUGGESTED BET: TAYLORS FOUR (8) each way.

BIGBASHASH (5) has gate speed and may look to press forward in the early stages of this race from a reasonable draw. He was running on nicely late into fourth last time out behind Camerina. TIMMYTEO (7) trialled up recently behind Captain Shuffles when running through the line reasonably late. He is likely to have derived good benefit from that outing and does appear the class runner in this race. ALL EYES ON BLING (2) has good gate speed and should be able to zip across before picking which horse she sits on. She elected to take a sit on Denver Colorado last time out who just didn’t quite have her hitting the sprint lane with momentum in a race taken out by Keayang Kauana. MULLUM RUBY (10) should get a good run off the speed in this race from a soft trailing draw. She was hitting the line nicely late behind Tralee Snickas last time out and is likely to have derived benefit from the run. SELECTIONS: BIGBASHASH (5), TIMMYTEO (7), ALL EYES ON BLING (2), MULLUM RUBY (10) SUGGESTED BET: BIGBASHASH (5) to win.

LOUARK (1) showed good gate speed last time out and was able to lead all the way there scoring quite impressively. He draws favourably again in this race and should be hard to beat despite the step up in grade. BETTOR BE BOHDI (8) loomed up and looked the winner last time out but was just nabbed on the line by Camerina who was able to kick back there and score. He should get a similar run in this race and will be hard to hold out. TORO LOCO (5) loomed into the race strongly last time out but just couldn’t quite reel in So Many Moments late over the 2138. He draws a touch awkwardly this time wider on the track and may be forced to do some work or could be shuffled back early. MAYWYN VALENTINO (4) was able to break through for another win recently at Redcliffe when working into the clear and sprinting nicely to beat Mitchells run and Same Old Devil. He should get a good run off the speed and can be running on. SELECTIONS: LOUARK (1), BETTOR BE BOHDI (8), TORO LOCO (5), MAYWYN VALENTINO (4) SUGGESTED BET: LOUARK (1) to win.

VINKE B (3) trialled up reasonably recently when well beaten by a smart horse in Captain Shuffles who ran a very slick last half. He joins the stable of Shawn Grimsey and should be ready to run a good race on stable debut. If he could find the lead early he would give them something to catch. BARRACUDA (5) wasn’t beaten far last time out in a strong race taken out by Fire And Passion. He draws a touch awkwardly and could be shuffled back in the early stages but if the race is run to suit he should be right in the finish again. MAJOR CRUNCH (7) was able to score a good win last time out running on from off the speed at Redcliffe over the 2040 rating good time. He draws awkwardly in this race and may be shuffled back in the early stages. DOLLY ROCKET (1) doesn’t have much gate speed and may be shuffled back a touch early. She was shuffled back early recently and was able to run on strongly into second behind Tizzie Lizzy over the 1660 at this track. SELECTIONS: VINKE B (3), BARRACUDA (5), MAJOR CRUNCH (7), DOLLY ROCKET (1) SUGGESTED BET: VINKE B (3) to win.

EXIT ELEVEN (6) secured a good run on the leaders back last time out and was able to show an electric turn of speed once working into the clear to dash past them late and score well. He has the draw advantage in this race over his key rival AARDIES A STAR (7) and may look to hold that advantage early in the race. AARDIES A STAR (7) draws poorly outside the front row but does appear the class runner of the field having run sixth in the Protostar two race starts ago. She was shuffled back early on resumption at this track and trip and worked through the line nicely late into third behind Bettor One and Blackjack Sam. WALK WITH ELEGANCE (9) trialled up very impressively when beaten just 10m by Shards Eclipse who rated very fast time. She looks likely to get a good run off the speed in this race and can be running into it late. FORGING ON (1) is very well bred being a half relation to Free Thinker, Future Assured, Fact Finder and French Fries. He appeared to finish his latest trial off impressively in a race which was run upside down there with a very quick first half being set by the Protostar winner Havtimemajor. SELECTIONS: EXIT ELEVEN (6), AARDIES A STAR (7), WALK WITH ELEGANCE (9), FORGING ON (1) SUGGESTED BET: EXIT ELEVEN (6) to win.

WHY TANYA SUE (8) retuned very impressively from a spell two starts ago when overcoming a 20m handicap sprinting nicely and scoring a big win. She made a break in her latest outing at Marburg. If she can bring her best manners in this race she should run well again and is likely to her derived good benefit from her two latest outings given she was resuming off a long spell. ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (4) secured a good run behind the speed two starts ago and ran on nicely into second behind WHY TANYA SUE (8). If she can step safely and settle close in the run she can play a part in the finish again. SMOKEY BEAR (1) looks well handicapped in this race. He led two starts ago and ran well there finishing third behind Moreep. He will be looking to step safely early and will have options from there. LIZZIES SON (9) will be looking for a hat-trick of wins in this race after leading all the way in his latest outing. He faces a 20m handicap this time and finds a slightly stronger field but is racing well and has to be respected. SELECTIONS: WHY TANYA SUE (8), ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (4), SMOKEY BEAR (1), LIZZIES SON (9) SUGGESTED BET: WHY TANYA SUE (8) to win.

ICONIC IMAGE (3) has gate speed and may look to press forward and find the lead early in this race. He was excellent last time out when overcoming a 30m handicap to finish second behind Fredidrivsamercy. He should be hard to beat. DESIRING DIAMONDS (1) had a big handicap advantage on a number of her key rivals last time out and was able to lead running well for a close up third. She starts on equal terms this time but should settle close enough in the run and should be thereabouts again. SERENA LOVE (4) is racing well but does appear to draw quite awkwardly in this race and may be left to do the work in the early stages of the race. She secured a good run two starts ago and just couldn’t quite reel in the leader late in a race which became a dash home taken out by Second To Nun. NONIS GOLD CLASS (2) looks likely to be able to tuck in just behind the speed in this race and can be looking to run into the minor money late. She secured a good run just behind the speed last time out and battled away well enough there for fourth. SELECTIONS: ICONIC IMAGE (3), DESIRING DIAMONDS (1), SERENA LOVE (4), NONIS GOLD CLASS (2) SUGGESTED BET: ICONIC IMAGE (3) to win.

SUNDAY SWEET TALK (5) looked very impressive again last time out when setting a moderate tempo before dashing up nicely late to hold off the challenge of IM FRANKEE (6). She is likely to have derived a lot of benefit from her first two outings and can run well again third up despite the increasing handicap. IM FRANKEE (6) ran a good race for second behind SUNDAY SWEET TALK (5) last time out overcoming a 40m handicap there to not be beaten far. Although she is now better suited the way the handicaps fall in this race her key rival is still likely to take some catching with a 20m head start. POZZI TONOZZI (4) was able to run a good third last time out behind the two likely fancied runners in this race. She should settle close enough and can be looking to run into third again in this race. STREAK APPEAL (2) secured a good run close to the speed last time out and battled on reasonably for fourth. She is likely to have derived benefit from her latest two outings and can run well again third up. SELECTIONS: SUNDAY SWEET TALK (5), IM FRANKEE (6), POZZI TONOZZI (4), STREAK APPEAL (2) SUGGESTED BET: SUNDAY SWEET TALK (5) to win. OVERVIEW:KING KASEY (3) is a fast beginner and has been recording fast times at his recent victories so he will take catching if he can find the lead. JOE GOT ROLLED (1) is rising in class on his past two runner up performances but he is a speedy type and is likely to gain the perfect trip behind the leader so he must be respected. WOTDIDUSAAAY (9) races best when he is able to lead so being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage but he is racing too well to dismiss. He recorded victories at Echuca and Cranbourne, missed out at Melton then performed nicely at a Melton trial third since. The interesting runner is the former New Zealand pacer AMALFI (11) for trainer Carson Millar. He is poorly drawn but his form across the Tasman is strong enough to suggest he can be competitive and he was placed in two Melton trials back in September. OCEAN AVENUE (7) produced a career best performance when second in a strong race at Melton last outing and is not without a chance in a quality field. SELECTIONS: KING KASEY (3), JOE GOT ROLLED (1), WOTDIDUSAAAY (9), AMALFI (11)

OVERVIEW:BRAVE ART (9) began quickly to lead and was taken on early with the first quarter being a sensational 26.5 seconds so her effort to finish third at Ballarat last outing was very brave. She appears to be well graded in this event and should prove very hard to beat. TUKURUA (3) is resuming since March but she was competing against much stronger opposition when she was last in work. She is nicely drawn first up and should run a good race. TORQUE INTHEUSA (7) was confidently supported and ran a cheeky race after working to the front when second at Hamilton last week. He is not as well drawn for this assignment but is worth thought again. PRETTY BASIC (8) was resuming since a Hamilton victory in April when fifth behind My Atlantis last week. He should be fitter from that performance and is worth following. BACK: BRAVE ART (9) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BRAVE ART (9), TUKURUA (3), TORQUE INTHEUSA (7), PRETTY BASIC (8)

OVERVIEW: MYDEEPESTDESIRE (6) is a strong type, which has been placed in four of her five starts to date and deserves to break through for a win. She raced without cover throughout when third behind Pet Wolf in a slick mile rate of 1.54.9 at Melton two starts ago, which is a good form pointer for this event. BANGBANG BOBBIE (7) is backing up quickly from his effort at St Arnaud on Sunday but his form is good enough to be competitive here. He finished second behind the smart juvenile pacer Lambro Louella at Mount Gambier on October 30. SUBATOMIC (2) ran into a distant second behind Witha Bitta Luck at Mount Gambier when on debut and is worth a place ticket from her good draw. JOKIC (5) is resuming since a debut fifth a Bendigo in May. He has performed fairly well at the trials with a win and a third at Maryborough to his credit and he is worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: MYDEEPESTDESIRE (6) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MYDEEPESTDESIRE (6), BANGBANG BOBBIE (7), SUBATOMIC (2), JOKIC (5)

OVERVIEW: ANOTHER WOODS (8) is resuming since an unplaced effort at Geelong in June but will be fitter for a recent unplaced Terang trial performance. He ran some big races against handy grade during his last preparation and recorded a mile rate of 1.55.5 at his last victory so he should be competitive if he is somewhere near his peak. FIVE CENT (6) raced without cover throughout when a creditable third behind Assigned two starts ago. He is a strong staying type and is worth thought under these conditions. BOBBYS ROOM (2) was held up for a run at a vital stage when a handy third behind Huxham Chubb last outing. He should be ready to strike his peak form after having two starts back from a break and is drawn to go well. A ROCKNROLL JET (1) battled on nicely after racing without cover throughout when fifth at Charlton last outing. He is much better drawn for this assignment and is capable of improving on his numerical form. SELECTIONS: ANOTHER WOODS (8), FIVE CENT (6), BOBBYS ROOM (2), A ROCKNROLL JET (1)

OVERVIEW:BUBBLE OVER (2) was resuming since May when she finished off nicely for third in fast final sectionals behind Colosimo at Terang. She should be better after that performance and is drawn to go close. MY FATAL CHARM (1) is a former Tasmanian pacer, which joins trainer Carson Millar. She is ideally drawn and was placed behind the handy pacer Our Ultimate Gracy two starts ago so she must be kept safe. MAJOR ROY (3) is a tough campaigner, which should make his presence felt. He trailed the leader and chased hard when a close second behind Billys Tiger Khan at Ballarat two starts ago. DARETODANCE (6) and MISSMALACHITE (7) are both racing well enough to figure in the finish despite being drawn widely. SELECTIONS: BUBBLE OVER (2), MY FATAL CHARM (1), MAJOR ROY (3), MISSMALACHITE (7)

OVERVIEW:CHILLHUNNYBUNNY (8) is a tough type and should be competitive against this line up. She raced without cover and got the better of Nedza Thriller to win at Ballarat three starts ago and went down fighting at Maryborough last outing. BETSY ANNE (5) led out then took cover mid-race when she got up to win at Maryborough last outing. She has been placed at her past four attempts and is worth thought again. ALLWATFUNJINGLES (6) is backing up quickly from his effort at Melton on Friday but he finished off well for second at Melton on October 23 so he is not without a chance. BROWN EYED KATE (2) has been placed in two of her past four starts and she is drawn to gain a trail just off the speed so she is worth thought. SELECTIONS: CHILLHUNNYBUNNY (8), BETSY ANNE (5), ALLWATFUNJINGLES (6), BROWN EYED KATE (2)

OVERVIEW: DESERT VIPER (3) was performing well at the trials prior a handy debut fourth behind Whitering, where she raced without cover throughout. She should have benefited from the experience and is worth thought again. CARPOPHORUS (8) is a former Queenslander, which was resuming since April when an eye-catching sixth at his Victorian debut, where he finished quickly from last. He is yet to be placed in 16 starts but his first up run was encouraging and he warrants respect. SINCEILEFTYOU (4) is a nicely bred first starter, which scored at a Melton trial effort last week and has the ability to give a forward showing. PETITE FOUR (2) finished a distant fourth when resuming at Charlton and is a minor place possibility from her good draw. SELECTIONS: DESERT VIPER (3), CARPOPHORUS (8), SINCEILEFTYOU (4), PETITE FOUR (2)

OVERVIEW: SMOKEN STREPO (6) produced a career best performance when he led throughout and scored by a large margin in a mile rate of 1.57.2 at Terang two starts ago. He is a short course specialist and should give a forward showing. NORMANDY NUGGET (2) performs best when he is close to the speed so he is perfectly drawn to suit his racing patten. He led throughout at a Ballarat victory on October 07. DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1) led throughout when he defeated Dulcie Maureen at Charlton last week and is worth thought again from the pole position despite rising in class. LIVERMERE (4) is a very quick beginner and has been placed in all three starts since resuming. She attempted to lead throughout when a close up third at Mount Gambier last outing. BACK: SMOKEN STREPO (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SMOKEN STREPO (6), NORMANDY NUGGET (2), DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1), LIVERMERE (4)

OVERVIEW: ROBERT JOHN (5) was resuming since July when he finished off well for a close second behind Massif Central at Maryborough. He won twice in succession towards the end of his last campaign and he should prove hard to beat again. MATISOFF (6) settled in the second half of the field and came out three horses wide from the 800m when he sustained the run to finish a creditable third behind Dance Fighter at Maryborough last week. A repeat performance will see him going close to winning here. ITGETSBETTER (1) did all of the work in the run and proved to be too strong at Mount Gambier last outing. This is a race of more depth but he is drawn to go well again. MAORIS RETURN (4) ran a game race for second at Horsham when resuming then couldn’t work into the race from a poor draw at Maryborough. He should be reaching his peak form after having two runs back from a spell and is not without a chance. BACK: ROBERT JOHN (5) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: ROBERT JOHN (5), MATISOFF (6), ITGETSBETTER (1), MAORIS RETURN (4)

An intriguing small stand-start field kicks off tonight, where TULLAH GIRL (4) looks well placed off the 10 metres. She was narrowly beaten here two starts ago before being somewhat disappointing last week, but in the small field you would expect her to get her chance to run over the top of them. ONEHANDONEBOUNCE (5) brings similar form lines and is another who should appreciate the small field after a handy third when doing all the work three wide two starts back. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (6) is clearly the class horse of the field, and if he begins as swiftly as he can, he may be able to make up the ground very quickly and be driven confidently here. FLEETWOOD ROCK (2) was well backed but galloped out at the same venue two starts ago, although a better beginning could leave him as a rough hope here. DENNY (1) isn't going as badly as his form suggests and should get his chance from the pole draw off the front mark. Selections: TULLAH GIRL (4), ONEHANDONEBOUNCE (5), ROCKANDHARDPLACE (6), FLEETWOOD ROCK (2) Staking Strategy: TULLAH GIRL looks to get her chance again here. 2 unit win – TULLAH GIRL (4)

OUTBACK LASS (1) drew the pole and was an easy winner against a similar field last start, so will look to replicate that performance again here. FEELINKINDALUCKY (6) should get his chance following her everywhere she goes and should appreciate getting back to the pegs close to the speed. TUFFTIGER (4) was good first up for the new stable but draws an awkward gate here. Expect they may roll forward and try dictate the speed outside the expected leader and favourite. PARK LANE (7) will have to be driven more conservatively this week from the back row but could run into a placing if the race becomes pegs dominated, which may make it difficult for the rest of the field to get into the finish. Selections: OUTBACK LASS (1), FEELINKINDALUCKY (6), TUFFTIGER (4), PARK LANE (7) Staking Strategy: No reason OUTBACK LASS cant lead and win again. 3 unit win – OUTBACK LASS (1).

GEMMY LOU (1) battled on gamely last start at the same track and distance but draws the ideal pole position here, which should make her extremely hard to beat. More than confident she can lead all the way. KING BART (3) drops back somewhat in grade and should find a spot on speed, which should see him right in the finish. OUR SWEET TRIXIE (8) has been racing consistently in stronger races than what she meets here and, although she will likely have to come with one run, can't be ruled out. IDEN REGAL WAVE (6) and STANTON BREAK (7) will look to duck to the pegs and hope the gaps appear late, which would give them both first-four chances. Selections: GEMMY LOU (1), KING BART (3), OUR SWEET TRIXIE (8), IDEN REGAL WAVE (6) Staking Strategy: GEMMY LOU looks extremely hard to beat off her last-start performance and with the aid of the inside gate. 4 unit win – GEMMY LOU (1).

Another race where the pole marker BABY CHARLOTTE (1) looks extremely hard to beat. Her recent effort when doing all the work outside the leader in handy time and sticking on well for second should make her very hard to beat here. Expect she should have enough gate speed to hunt through early and hold the front, and even over the middle distance, she clearly looks the one to beat. HIGH FROSTY (5) was well backed and a dominant winner first up at this track, aided by some solid mid-race tempo. From the draw, he will need something similar here, but expect him to be running home strongly yet again. OSCAR MAC (6) should follow the expected favourite everywhere she goes and gets his chance to run into a placing, while VITESSE (3) is a four-year-old mare on debut whose two trials thus far have been handy enough. Expect her to put some wins together soon for her patient connections. Selections: BABY CHARLOTTE (1), HIGH FROSTY (5), OSCAR MAC (6), VITESSE (3) Staking Strategy: BABY CHARLOTTE only needs to kick up enough early to hold the front and will be hard to run down on her local track. 3 unit win – BABY CHARLOTTE (1).

Another stand-start event where manners will be key, but it is hard to go past LIKEABLE ROGUE (2) after his last-start victory, when an easy winner in the heat of this race. In the bigger field, he will need to be on his best behaviour and step away safely this time, but from the draw he looks one of the better chances. MIKI SANZ (3) is always thereabouts in these sorts of races and expect him to sit on speed and run his usual honest race. SETTEBELLO (1) was somewhat disappointing in the heat when having every chance in front, but may get his chance to redeem himself with a quick beginning and give them something to chase at odds. The runners off the 10-metre handicap will need some pressure throughout to allow them to get into the finish, but can't be ruled out for exotics, led by MAJOR DAVVIN (8), who should benefit being second up from a decent break. Selections: LIKEABLE ROGUE (2), MIKI SANZ (3), SETTEBELLO (1), MAJOR DAVVIN (8), Staking Strategy: LIKEABLE ROGUE should be in the finish again with a safe beginning. 1 unit win – LIKEABLE ROGUE (2).

Expect some good tempo early here, with numerous horses possessing sharp gate speed engaged off the front row, which should again play into the hands of KENYA (8), who is threatening to break through after some good seconds of late. He was narrowly defeated in track-record time when coming with one run at them two starts ago at this track, and similar tactics should see him right in the firing line again. KNOCK OUT (7) gets the nice trailing draw and drops back in grade. If he puts his best foot forward, expect him to be running home strongly. SUMTHIN ELSE (1) gets the pole draw around the tight circuit and has her chance to improve, although she may cop some pressure from runners drawn wider. EYE SEE AMOUR (4) and QUEENOFDANCE (5) have been in good form of late but will need good drives and some luck in transit to be in the finish from their wide front-row draws. Selections: KENYA (8), KNOCK OUT (7), SUMTHIN ELSE (1), QUEENOFDANCE (5) Staking Strategy: KENYA should get his chance to run over the top off a hot tempo. 3 unit win – KENYA (8).

The standing-start event over the short trip, where CINCINNATI (1) will look to step cleanly from the tapes, as he did last start when second in a similar grade. He looked to have every chance that day when defeated by COLORADO GIRL (5), who won with somewhat ease and again draws the 10-metre mark here. A repeat performance from her would make her hard to hold out late. SMOOTH DEAL (2) is known for pinging the tapes and could run a race at odds if he finds the pegs first, although he will need to improve on his performance from last Sunday. RANIERI (3) and NO NUKES SKIPPER (8) look the best of the rest on current form. Selections: COLORADO GIRL (5), CINCINNATI (1), RANIERI (3), NO NUKES SKIPPER (8) Staking Strategy: CINCINNATI looks a safe each-way play in the race. 1 unit each-way – CINCINNATI (1).

The highest-class event of the night from behind the mobile, where SOHO TIGER LILY (1) and WEONA EAGLE (2), both possessing very sharp gate speed, draw well. You would expect SOHO TIGERLILY (1) to hold the front and she could take some running down. However, she has done her best racing over the mile trip, so if she cops pressure at any stage, she could become somewhat vulnerable late. FAMILY REASONS (3) and HAY MIKI (4) have been competing in stronger races than what they meet here and will be hoping to slot into the running line, where both should be in the finish if they hold their form. INTO THE HARKNESS (7) could be the one at odds if she puts her best foot forward, having run a good second behind a handy one two starts back. From the nice trailing back-row draw, she could be finishing strongly with some tempo throughout. Selections: FAMILY REASONS (3), SOHO TIGER LILY (1), INTO THE HARKNESS (7), WEONA EAGLE (2) Staking Strategy: FAMILY REASONS should sit on speed with cover and get his chance late. 2 unit win – FAMILY REASONS (3). The two-year-olds combine for the No More Than One Win event, where KOOKY (3) looks extremely hard to beat. She should have enough gate speed to zoom straight to the front, as she did last week in the Group 2 Evicus Final, when run down in the final 50 metres to finish second. A similar performance here would make her very hard to run down. VINCENT THE THIRD (1) showed good ability as an early two-year-old and produced a handy effort last start. He looks the one most likely to knock off the expected favourite if able to follow her everywhere around the pegs. MISS VINCENTINA (2) is going better than her overall form figures suggest, having not been beaten far behind some smart types in very fast time, and could be the one at odds running home strongly. MAJOR SCOTTY (4) and SOLO STITCH (5) have competed in feature races of late but will need to improve on those performances to be in the finish here. Selections: KOOKY (3), VINCENT THE THIRD (1), MISS VINCENTINA (2), MAJOR SCOTTY (4)

An extremely even event over the short trip, where you would expect EVERYTHING BUT THE (1) and IMPERIAL LAZ (3) to contest the early lead. EVERYTHING BETTOR (1) has been in great form working his way through the grades of late before battling against some very handy open class horses last week. If he backs up from that run, he should get every chance from the pole draw. IMPERIAL LAZ (3) copped interference last week when a late scratching but should be suited to the mile distance and, at his best, should be right in the finish. JOHN VINCENT (4) has been a consistent performer since arriving in the state and will look to settle just behind the speed before running home strongly. The rest of the field will be relying on some solid tempo early to allow them to run home over the top, where WE SALUTE YOU (8) looks the pick of them, getting his preferred pegs run. Selections: EVERYTHING BUT THE (1), IMPERIAL LAZ (3), JOHN VINCENT (4), WE SALUTE YOU (8)

COMINSKI LEIS (9) looks to get his chance to put another win on the board from the nice trailing back-row draw. BRIGHTLY BLAZE (5) draws an awkward gate but has been racing well whenever he gets the right run in transit, so will again be hoping for something similar here. VOODOO RANGER (1) and ARRIVAL TIME (3) have been consistently finishing in the minor placings and get draws to their advantage, giving them another chance to break their maiden status. ROCKNROLL MCRAE (7) could be the one at odds, having shown ability at times, but he draws an awkward gate here. Selections: COMINSKI LEIS (9),BRIGHTLY BLAZE (5), VOODOO RANGER (1), ROCKNROLL MCRAE

JILLIBY WORPA (2) was a dominant winner last start when finding the front and running slick time. He may cop some more pressure here from other horses off the front row, including A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3) and STORMZABREWEN (4), who were both good winners last start but draw outside him here. QUEEN ANAETASIA (7) has been racing well but draws an awkward gate, so may have to be driven more conservatively and hope for some genuine tempo throughout. SPORTZSILK (8) is threatening to break through but also draws awkwardly and will be relying on some luck and better manners to be in the finish. Similar could be said for ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (9), who got it all wrong in the score-up last start but, at his best, could easily be winning here. Selections: JILLIBY WORPA (2), ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (9), A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3), QUEEN ANASTASIA (7)

An extremely strong 75–105 event here, where CARMEN EMJAY (1) will be looking to use the barrier draw to her advantage. She should have sufficient gate speed to hold the front and, while she rises slightly in class against mostly Free For All horses, the times and sectionals she has been running when narrowly beaten from bad draws recently should make her very hard to run down. WAVES OF CHANCE (5) is expected to push forward from the wide gate to find a position on speed, while tactics could be interesting with his stablemate RAKADAN (7), who normally does his best racing on speed but draws the outside gate here. The class performers of the field include BETTABLACK TIGER (8), MAGICIAN (9) and THE SHALLOWS (10), who are all racing well and will be relying on some genuine tempo throughout to run home strongly into the finish. Selections: CARMEN EMJAY (1), BETTABLACK TIGER (8), MAGICIAN (9), THE SHALLOWS (10),

WHERE IT BEGAN (1) will be looking for back-to-back victories after winning at huge odds in fast time in the three-year-old Guineas last start. He should be able to hold the lead here and run at the tempo he desires, so there is no reason why he can't be winning again. PHLOW JO (2) is racing well and should find a position on speed, making her a genuine each-way chance, as does DOLCE DRAMA (4), who has been racing well without winning in similar grade to what she meets here. SPORT WATCHER (3) should again be looking to earn a cheque for connections from the handy draw, while ALWAYS AURORA (6) and REALLY SMARTIE (7) could be the ones at odds if they are able to get a nice cart into the race from their awkward front-row draws with some tempo on throughout. Selections: WHERE IT BEGAN (1), PHLOW JO (2), DOLCE DRAMA (4), SPORT WATCHER (3)

MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (2) will be looking to take advantage of a good front-row draw to be first to the pegs. SOLO SAFARI (3) broke last start, but his prior form in higher-class races would have him competitive here, and he gets his chance from the nice draw. KUHIO CREST (6) is going well but will need some luck from the wide draw and may look to push forward from the gate in what appears a moderate front row for gate speed. The back-row runners STAROFREMEMBRANCE (9) and DEBT TILL WE PART (10) will be running home strongly as usual if there is any genuine tempo throughout. Selections: MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (2), SOLO SAFARI (3), KUHIO CREST (6), DEBT TILL WE PART (10)

The final race of the day sees the class horses of the field drawn wide on the front row. REMMINGTON (5) was used early when the race was stopped and rerun last week, so happy to forgive that performance. Expect him to hunt forward from the gate and attempt to find the pegs, or at least a position on speed, and ensure a solid tempo throughout. Stablemates SNOWIEWILLREV (6) and IDEN OLIVER (7) bring the next strongest form into the race and look the main dangers, although they may be relying on some early tempo from the runners drawn inside to allow them to run home strongly. IAMAHUNTER (9) was well backed when saluting from the stand last week and, although rising slightly in class, should still be running home strongly into the finish. MONTGOMERY BURNS (8) has been thereabouts of late but will be relying on some luck from the inside back-row draw, while ROCKNALLOVERTHEWORLD (3) looks the best of the Wayne Yole-trained runners after a couple of handy efforts of late and will be looking to make use of his good front-row draw. Selections: REMMINGTON (5), SNOWIEWILLREV (6), IDEN OLIVER (7), IAMAHUNTER (9) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

PERFECT PLAYGIRL (4) has won two of her last three starts and has stepped it up another level. She defeated NORMY by a half neck on Monday. If she keeps racing the way she is racing she will be hard to beat. AFTER THE CHASE (5) looks like a big danger with Wayne Hill in the sulky. He is a lot better than his recent form. He could be a major improver tonight. NORMANS GIRL (2) and ALWAYS BE TECHY (1) are also chances.

SPLASH OF PAYNT (2) can be a very hard horse to follow at times but he does his best racing when he can lead. He is a good chance of finding the top early and he should be hard to catch over 1800 metres. DEE JAYS MISS (9), MAGIC STORM (8) and WHATA OPTIMST (1) are all big chances in an even race.

HEZ SO ROYAL (5) looks very hard to beat to beat tonight. He has had an excellent start to his racing career and he looks like the superior horse in this race. LE GASTON (7) has a Victorian record that must be respected. He is a big threat tonight. STEAM MACHINE (3) and FRANKIE UNDER FIRE (6) are also chances.

TREACHEROUS DAN (3) has won three of his last five starts. His recent form in Tasmania has been very strong. Emma Steward rarely loses here at Globe Derby. He is going to be very hard to beat. SRIRACHA (1) was an impressive winner at Melton last start and he has the inside draw on his side. He is a big threat. MICKTHEBESTBUTCHER (2) and SEABLASTER (4) look the next best.

MISS NASHVILLE (7) had a set back last start at Port Pirie when she galloped in the score up but made up a tonne of ground chasing. She has Ryan Hryhorec back in the sulky tonight who has a perfect record with her. She has race fitness on her side as well and hasn’t yet shown how good she truly is. She looks hard to beat tonight. HILLTOP BLOSSOM (1) must be respected tonight from the inside draw. She hasn’t had a run for 11 months but Emma Stewart runners must be respected here at Globe Derby. BAY LA VILLE (3) and BETTY CAROLINE (5) look the next best.

SANDLETON (1) has won two from her three career starts at Melton. She will love the inside draw and will be hard to beat if she can repeat those Melton runs. HILLTOP STAR (3) returns from a long spell but she rejoins the Emma Stewart stable. She is worth strong consideration. PARVATI (5) and MEZZANOTTI (4) are also chances.

LEVIOSA (5) looked special on debut when she defeated LAMBRO LOUELLA by a head. A repeat of that run will put her right in the finish tonight. WITHA BITTA LUCK (4) is another who looked special on debut at Mount Gambier when she defeated SUBATOMIC by 27.7 metres. Tonight will be tougher for her but she does look like a major chance. MY ROCKING HORSE (2) and CHIARA MARA (1) look the next best.

LAMBRO LOUELLA (5) has won her last two starts at Horsham and Mount Gambier. Her last run here at Globe Derby behind LEVIOSA was strong. She is a major chance tonight. KENZINGTON (1) hasn’t trialled in a spectacular fashion but her stable must be respected here from the inside draw. MYA QUICK (3) and SAL WESTER (4) look the next best. OVERVIEW:CHALKNCHEDDAR (5) settled three back on the markers and tried hard for third behind Talknplay at Swan Hill last outing. He appears to be very well placed against this field and is versatile enough to overcome the wide draw. STONEBRIDGE STAR (2) finished off fairly well for third behind Keayang Crippa at Mildura on October 20. This race is a little easier and he is worth thought again. DIAMOND KRUSHER (6) is a fast beginner and is a good chance of finding the lead despite being drawn on the outside of the front line. He led throughout at a Mildura victory on September 04 so he cannot be left out of calculations. BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (7) missed out at Swan Hill last week but he ran a very good race for second behind Talknplay (won again since) three starts ago so he is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: CHALKNCHEDDAR (5), STONEBRIDGE STAR (2), DIAMOND KRUSHER (6), BOHEMIAN BRAIDS (7)

OVERVIEW:LITLMAX (3) was driven with plenty of confidence on debut where she was headed off from the pole position and moved up without cover from the 1600m. She has ability and strikes a suitable field so she can go one better here. LATHER WITH FIRE (5) broke stride and lost her chance at her latest distant fourth but she has won a trial at Shepparton since and is a possible improver. CRUEL MISTRESS (6) finished off reasonably well from midfield when third behind Phils Boy in a race of similar standard last outing. She is widely drawn but is not without a chance. BRIEISBETTER (7) is an experienced maiden having had 65 attempts but she has been placed in two of her past three starts and she should enjoy an economical run from her trailing draw. BACK: LITLMAX (3) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: LITLMAX (3), LATHER WITH FIRE (5), CRUEL MISTRESS (6), BRIEISBETTER (7)

OVERVIEW: THE LADYBIRD (2) did very well after being in the uncharacteristic role of parking without cover at her latest Kilmore third. She recorded a mile rate of 1.57.7 when she scored at Horsham prior and she should prove hard to beat again. HESASTAR (3) is a fast beginner and should give a forward showing from his good draw. He worked forward to find the lead and scored comfortably at Mildura on September 18. KEAYANG CRIPPA (5) gained a nice trail and finished off best to snare victory over HESASTAR (3) last outing. He is usually competitive against this class and is worth thought again. ROJENBYE (8) picked up some ground from midfield when fourth at Charlton last outing and is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: THE LADYBIRD (2), HESASTAR (3), KEAYANG CRIPPA (5), ROJENBYE (8)

OVERVIEW: BRANSON (2) is a capable South Australian trained pacer, which led throughout to win in a mile rate of 1.57.3 at Gawler two starts ago. He is a good chance of finding the lead again and will take catching over the sprint distance. SUNSHINE WARRIOR (1) led throughout at a Mildura victory three starts ago and she didn’t have the best of luck from a wide alley at her latest fifth. She should receive the perfect trip from the pole position and is worth an investment. ASHANTE WARRIOR (7) is making his Mildura debut but his form in the South-East has been strong enough to be competitive against this class. He led throughout in a mile rate of 1.57.8 three starts ago. MASON DIXON LINE (3) hasn’t been able to draw on the front line for a long time so he gets his chance to improve under these conditions. SELECTIONS: BRANSON (2), SUNSHINE WARRIOR (1), ASHANTE WARRIOR (7), MASON DIXON LINE (3)

OVERVIEW:CELESTIAL STARLET (6) is a 2yo filly on debut but she has shaped up nicely at the trials with a win and a third at Maryborough to her credit. She obviously has ability and is likely to be strongly fancied. MISTER HENDRIX (5) has been unplaced in all of this three starts to date but his trial form is far stronger than his race form. He strikes a suitable assignment at his first run since March and he is worth respect. MISS CULLEN (7) trailed the leader and dropped out at the end when last of seven at Swan Hill last outing. She met a much stronger field last time out and was runner up at her previous two attempts so she must be considered as a place hope again. THE MIGHTY CAESAR (3) is a first starter for trainer Boris Devcic, which has had numerous trial attempts and is worth thought in multiple combinations. SELECTIONS: CELESTIAL STARLET (6), MISTER HENDRIX (5),MISS CULLEN (7), THE MIGHTY CAESAR (3)

OVERVIEW:RUFF NUT (6) progressed forward to race without cover and fought on strongly when a brave second behind Chase The Stars at Globe Derby last outing. He is a tough campaigner and looms as one of the leading chances. DALLAS MIKI (8) is a bold front running pacer, which is unsuited being drawn on the second row but is sure to make his presence felt. He was held up for a run at a vital stage and locked wheels momentarily turning for home when an unlucky fourth in the Swan Hill Cup last week. THE GOLDEN HOOK (7) is racing in career best form but this is his toughest test to date. He sustained a long run when he got up to defeat Keayang Shadowbox at Mildura last outing. ROYAL SAXON (3) settled in the second half of the field and tried to sustain a long run from the 800m when a game third at Mildura last outing. He should go well again from his good draw. SELECTIONS: RUFF NUT (6), DALLAS MIKI (8), THE GOLDEN HOOK (7), ROYAL SAXON (3)

OVERVIEW: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (5) settled in the second half of the field and finished off strongly for a game third in the Swan Hill Cup last week. He led throughout to win comfortably when resuming at Mildura on September 30 and is clearly the horse to beat again. HOT DEAL (7) commenced from the inside of the second line, was held up behind tiring runners and finished off fairly well for fifth at Globe Derby last outing. He boasts a very strong record at Mildura and will run his usual honest race if he has normal luck in running from the awkward draw. PRIORITISE (8) settled in the second half of the field, came out three horses wide over the latter stages and produced a strong finish to win at Mildura last outing. This race is of similar standard and he looms as one of the leading chances again. MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (1) is a strong pacer, which will take tossing if he can hold a forward position at the start. He was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off solidly for a close up third at Swan Hill last outing. BACK: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MY ULTIMATE JIMMY (5), HOT DEAL (7), PRIORITISE (8), MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (1)

OVERVIEW: ARMOURY (6) is a former New South Wales pacer, which joins trainer Alex Ashwood. She was shuffled back in the field mid-race and failed to run on at Penrith last outing but was a winner on that track three starts ago and strikes a suitable assignment at her Mildura debut. EAGLEYE (1) has been placed in four of her past five starts and is perfectly drawn to run a good race again. She commenced from the inside of the second line, was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off well for second at Swan Hill last outing. LORD MYRMECIA (8) failed to run on as expected at Kapunda last outing but he finished fast for an eye-catching second at Globe Derby prior and has performed well at Mildura previously so he cannot be left out of calculations. CELESTIAL NEBULAE (10) has the ability to figure in the finish but he wanted to hang in badly on the bends at Globe Derby last outing so being drawn on the second line will be a disadvantage. SELECTIONS: ARMOURY (6), EAGLEYE (1), LORD MYRMECIA (8), CELESTIAL NEBULAE (10)

OVERVIEW: BETTORBUST (3) finished second behind the smart pacer Delizioso at Shepparton last outing and was a runaway winner at Mildura prior. He is the class runner of the field and will prove extremely hard to beat. CAULONIA TERROR (4) settled three back on the markers, got caught up behind tiring horses and lost approximately five lengths with 700m remaining so he did well to recover and finish in third behind Lower Manhattan last outing. He was unlucky in that performance and is worth a ticket each way. FLAME BLASTER (2) performs best when he is able to trail the leader so he is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern. He was runner up from behind the leader last outing and is a strong place chance again. OZZIE DAYBREAK (9) has performed extremely well in two starts back from a spell and rates as a value hope. BACK: BETTORBUST (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETTORBUST (3), CAULONIA TERROR (4), FLAME BLASTER (2), OZZIE DAYBREAK (9)

OVERVIEW: BANDIT EYES (9) endured a tough run and dropped out at Metropolitan level last outing. He led throughout to score in a sizzling mile rate of 1.53.2 at Melton back in August and is the class runner of this field. MIDNIGHT PIRATE (2) was caught wide early, restrained to being five back on the markers mid-race and worked home well for fourth at Swan Hill last outing. He is a fast beginner and is racing in good form so a bold showing is expected. HAPPY AS CAN BE (5) competed in the South Australian Cup series, where seventh in the Final so he is likely to find this race to be easier. He had his chance when second at Globe Derby last week but warrants consideration. SHIRLEY NOT (6) is racing in career best form and is worth thought along with the handy sprinter GOOD BOOTS BINDI (7). BACK: BANDIT EYES (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BANDIT EYES (9), MIDNIGHT PIRATE (2), HAPPY AS CAN BE (5), GOOD BOOTS BINDI (7)

OVERVIEW:FLEUR BELLA (1) won twice in succession at Mildura prior to a sixth at Swan Hill, where she led out then took cover. She is a fast beginner and she boasts the terrific record of three wins from six starts on the track so she warrants respect. CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (3) began very quickly from a wide draw and ran along at a genuine tempo when he scored at Globe Derby last outing. He is drawn to obtain a prominent position again and is worth an investment. ROJENBYE (7) has the perfect trailing draw behind FLEUR BELLA (1) and is worth a ticket each way. SNEAKY PHILTRA (9) is a versatile mare and recorded a victory at Mildura against similar opposition on October 06 so she cannot be left out of calculations. SELECTIONS: FLEUR BELLA (1), CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (3), ROJENBYE (7), SNEAKY PHILTRA (9)

OVERVIEW:THE LADYBIRD (10) recorded a handy mile rate of 1.57.7 when she scored at Horsham three starts ago and appears to be well placed against this line up. She is capable of sprinting to the line quickly with the right trail forward so being drawn on the second line isn’t a big disadvantage. DAYSIE BROWN (7) will be relying on ELISSAS DELIGHT (1) holding a forward position at the start but her form last preparation would suggest she is capable of being very competitive. DIAMOND KRUSHER (8) was a winner at Mildura on September 04 after she led throughout. She has done well at Mildura this season and has claims despite being drawn on the second line. ELISSAS DELIGHT (1) is a fast beginner and finished fourth after setting the speed over the longer distance two starts ago so she is capable of filling a place. SELECTIONS: THE LADYBIRD (10), DAYSIE BROWN (7), DIAMOND KRUSHER (8), ELISSAS DELIGHT (1)

OVERVIEW: OUR MONARCH (4) is a South Australian trained pacer, which won a trial at Globe Derby then followed with a third at a Gawler trial performance in handy time. She obviously has ability and strikes a suitable assignment first up. ALWAYS BENEFITS (2) was resuming since June when he worked home well from midfield and finished fourth behind Kaidenboy at Charlton. He is better drawn for this assignment and is not without a chance. LITLMAX (6) is backing up quickly from her performance at Mildura on Friday but she was confidently driven when second at her debut performance and has the ability to feature prominently. LATHER WITH FIRE (10) is also backing up quickly from Friday afternoon’s Mildura meeting and she won a trial at Shepparton prior so she cannot be dismissed. BACK: OUR MONARCH (4) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: OUR MONARCH (4), ALWAYS BENEFITS (2), LITLMAX (6), LATHER WITH FIRE (10)

OVERVIEW: ACCELERE (5) is yet to miss a place in seven starts for the season and should run his usual honest race. He worked hard from a similar wide draw to find the lead and battled on nicely for second behind the smart juvenile pacer Bettorbust at Mildura last outing. HOOKLINEANDSINKER (6) suffered atrial fibrillation and was retired out of the race at Mildura last outing. He recorded handy time after working forward to find the front at Globe Derby prior so he is worth another chance. LORD MYRMECIA (1) finished off fast when an eye-catching second at Globe Derby on September 22. He is ideally drawn and looms as one of the leading chances. The South Australian trained pacers TWO WAY WONDER (3) and HARLEM TOWN (4) are both worth thought despite being unplaced at their past few attempts and CALF PEN (7) is usually competitive against this class. BACK: ACCELERE (5) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: ACCELERE (5), HOOKLINEANDSINKER (6), LORD MYRMECIA (1), TWO WAY WONDER (3)

OVERVIEW:BAZZAS LEGACY (4) is racing consistently and deserves to break through for a win. He finished third behind Tooram Danny in a stronger race at Swan Hill three starts ago, which is a strong form pointer for this event. WINSHEMAY (9) is the only horse in this race that wasn’t nominated for Friday afternoon’s meeting. She was impressive when winning on debut and was runner up behind the tightly assessed performer Noble Trick at a recent trial effort so she must be respected. KEAYANG SHADOWBOX (8) has been steadily working back into his best form and strikes a winnable assignment now. He wasn’t beaten by far when second behind the classy pacer The Golden Hook at Mildura on October 20. HELLAVA DEAL (7) was competing against stronger opposition when she was last in work. She is awkwardly drawn but should be finding the line well. SELECTIONS: BAZZAS LEGACY (4), WINSHEMAY (9), KEAYANG SHADOWBOX (8), HELLAVA DEAL (7)

OVERVIEW:CEMETERY BAY (1) has been competing against the open class pacers at Mildura and appears to be well graded in this event. His last win at Mildura was in a much harder race (National Rating 60-75) back in August and he is perfectly drawn for this assignment. GOOD BOOTS BINDI (2) is a handy sprinter and is perfectly drawn to gain a trail just behind the speed so she should be dangerous at the end. SHIRLEY NOT (3) has been racing in career best form with three recent Mildura victories to her credit. She is stepping up in grade but she is versatile and should make her presence felt. ROYAL SAXON (6) will need some luck from the wide draw but he ran a strong race for third behind SHIRLEY NOT (3) on October 20 and will go well with normal luck in running. BACK: CEMETERY BAY (1) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: CEMETERY BAY (1), GOOD BOOTS BINDI (2), SHIRLEY NOT (3), ROYAL SAXON (6)

OVERVIEW: HAPPY AS CAN BE (3) finished fourth in a heat of the South Australian Cup then followed with a seventh in the Final. He will enjoy racing against this class and is drawn to go close. CAULONIA TERROR (5) was a winner at Mildura on September 18 and he was unlucky behind Lower Manhattan two starts ago as he was held up behind tiring horses at the 700m mark. He is likely to settle in the second half of the field from his awkward alley but he should be hitting the line strongly. MY ULTIMATE BILLY (2) was placed behind the in-form pacer The Golden Hook two starts ago and wasn’t far away at his latest fifth. He is worth a ticket each way from his good draw. FOXY TWO GLOVES (4) led out then took cover when a game second behind the Emma Stewart prepared Star Vision on Swan Hill Cup night so a bold showing is expected. SELECTIONS: HAPPY AS CAN BE (3), CAULONIA TERROR (5), MY ULTIMATE BILLY (2), FOXY TWO GLOVES (4)

OVERVIEW: SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (1) performed very well at the trials prior to a third behind the smart South Australian pacer Rankine when resuming. He should be building on his fitness and will take beating from the pole position. EAGLEYE (2) has been racing very consistently and ran a game race behind Talknplay at Swan Hill two starts ago, where she was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off solidly. This race is no harder and she worth thought again. HILLTOP CRUNCH (8) has remained undefeated in two starts since resuming from a break and should gain an economical run from his trailing draw so there is no reason why he can’t win again. CLARENDEN ARCADIA (3) and MY ULTIMATE HENRY (6) are both racing well enough to figure in the finish. BACK: SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (1) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: SHUDABOUGHTABOAT (1), EAGLEYE (2), HILLTOP CRUNCH (8), MY ULTIMATE HENRY (6)

OVERVIEW: First heat of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup here where plenty can win, but I’ll side with ANAKIN (2) for Team Shinn. He has been caught parked his last two at Kilmore, but boxed on bravely to not be beaten far. If he can find the fence, he should be fighting out the finish as his best is pretty good in this grade. TED BEAR (3) was a good winner at Melton last time out and all his recent form is sound, GENERAL ROCKER (6) ran well first-up for trainer Glenn Beale to only be beaten 10.8m in a fast race at Kilmore on October 22 and might be one to consider at likely good odds, while COOL STORY (10) dug deep to win as favourite from the chair at Ballarat back on October 7 and is certainly a winning chance with the right trip and tempo from wide on the back line. SELECTIONS: ANAKIN (2), TED BEAR (3), GENERAL ROCKER (6), COOL STORY (10)

OVERVIEW: RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (4) has been very close to breaking his maiden on a number of occasions and is presented with another great chance here. He has done things wrong in recent starts but has still managed close-up minor placings his last four outings and certainly looks capable of taking a race like this on his best behaviour. COGNAC COWBOY (1) produced a big finale from back in the field to just miss last start at Kilmore and draws for a lovely trip here, DIAMOND CHIPP (3) finished alongside RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (4) at Geelong two back and wasn’t too bad when fourth last start at Kilmore, while HILLCROFT HUSTLER (7) was good on debut when second to a handy one in Winchester Boy at Cranbourne and is among the winning chances alongside BAD GRANDMA (6) and perhaps BANIA (9), who trialled well and started odds-on on debut at Geelong but dropped out sharply after a tough trip last time at Melton. SELECTIONS: RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (4), COGNAC COWBOY (1), DIAMOND CHIPP (3), HILLCROFT HUSTLER (7)

OVERVIEW: OUR TINKA BELLE (6) is a five-year-old who only made her debut back in July, but has shown loads of ability despite plenty of issues with her manners. Two back at Geelong, she looked home in the straight at massive odds before galloping in the shadows of the post. And last time at Kilmore, she was held up in the last lap but unleashed a big finale to round up her rivals and win softly on the line under minimal driving from Jack Laugher. She’s taking on much more experienced rivals in this Bacchus Marsh Trotters Cup heat, but I think there’s some good ability there. DOSSIER (9) drops back slightly in grade and brings in some strong formlines, stablemate JOE LOU (7) has loads of talent but has broken his last two and is a risky trotter, while JAKARTA (10) has been competitive of late and is the highest rated trotter in the field at 55 so must be respected. BACK: OUR TINKA BELLE (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: OUR TINKA BELLE (6), DOSSIER (9), JOE LOU (7), JAKARTA (10)

OVERVIEW: WEONA OUR RIGHTS (8) has been in good form for Adam Shaw in recent weeks with a string of close-up efforts at Cranbourne and Melton. Last time, he was only beaten 5.7m into second by the handy Kosimo and had chased home in-form rivals such as Quick Crunch, Cyclone Jenni and Blazin By before that. Just needs the right trip to be going close, and he might get it if ANIMADO (1) kicks up and holds the top. ANIMADO (1) settled at the rear of the field from a wide barrier and charged late to be beaten just a head at Shepparton last time out. It was a good effort, and from the pole draw he’s a chance at start 150. ROSBERG (2) seems to often end up racing in the chair, but did win from that position in good style at Melton back in late September, while MIDNIGHT MOJO (5) is racing consistently well of late and is another of the key winning chances alongside FLIGHT LOUTENANT (7). BACK: WEONA OUR RIGHTS (8) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: WEONA OUR RIGHTS (8), ANIMADO (1), ROSBERG (2), MIDNIGHT MOJO (5)

OVERVIEW: Second heat of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup and it’s another wide-open event where most of the runners have claims. QUICK CRUNCH (8) brings in the winning form following back-to-back triumphs at Cranbourne and Ballarat, and looks a good chance of making it three on end despite the inside back row draw. She has run solid last halves in both those victories from the fence and should be fighting out the finish. SPORTS NARRATOR (9) was probably only fair first-up from a break at Ballarat on October 29 when fifth to Master Louey but ran some good races late last campaign and looks capable in this grade, FOREGONE CONCLUSION (2) just missed at Kilmore last time when coming from back in the field and is a very honest customer who has won 26 career races, while CORNISHTOWN KID (5) has been going okay of late in perhaps slightly stronger company and can figure with the right trip. SELECTIONS: QUICK CRUNCH (8), SPORTS NARRATOR (9), FOREGONE CONCLUSION (2), CORNISHTOWN KID (5)

OVERVIEW: WHIRLY MAURZ (3) has a runner-up placing and dominant victory to her name since joining the Andy Gath stable, and will likely go around as a warm favourite in this clash. Last week at Ballarat, she settled in the one-one and bolted away from her rivals – including IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1) and THE MOUNTAIN (5) – to break her maiden by a huge margin at start 34. She can win again in this company. RIDDLEMETHIS (7) looks the key danger to her chances after a good three-start campaign so far. He managed two placings at Kilmore and a tough Ballarat win through October and should run well despite the wide gate. FREAK OUT (4) and IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1) are next best, but a result outside the top two fancies would surprise. SELECTIONS: WHIRLY MAURZ (3), RIDDLEMETHIS (7), FREAK OUT (4), IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1)

OVERVIEW: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (2) has started her latest campaign with back-to-back victories at Geelong and Melton, and this shapes as another very winnable assignment. She was a tad lucky to score at Geelong when the leader galloped in the shadows of the post, but her latest effort when parked at Melton was outstanding. She charged clear there and won softly by 18.2m in a dominant performance. Happy her way. KISS AT MIDNIGHT (4) probably has the speed to lead this race, but her manners have been awful in recent times with gallops in the past four outings. Her best is good enough, but she’s very hard to trust at the moment. MAJESTIC CHARMA (6) led and faded late in what was just a fair effort last time at Maryborough but has won seven career races and two this campaign, while AI SEDHAI (3) and AHUNDREDPLUS (5) might be best of the rest, but victory would probably surprise. BACK: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (2) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE (2), KISS AT MIDNIGHT (4), MAJESTIC CHARMA (6), AI SEDHAI (3)

OVERVIEW: Tough way to end the night at Melton, but REASON TO LAUGH (7) gets the nod despite the wide front row draw. Last start at Ballarat, he was trapped three wide for the last lap but actually did a great job to soldier on and only be beaten 7.5m in a slick enough last half for this grade of 57.7sec. The run before that was a well-beaten second to handy rival Talknplay, and there are good wins earlier in the month at Cranbourne and Kilmore through his recent form. ARE WEASLEY (5) is another of the leading contenders after finding the winner’s stall at his last outing at Kilmore when closing off nicely from the one-one for Connor Clarke, there’s a big watch on MAMMALS BLAZE (6) who is now in the care of trainer Joe Pace and won his first trial for the stable at Bacchus Marsh in preparation for this, while GOZO MAJOR (4) and OUR TRUE COLOURS (3) are other hopes in an even contest to close the meeting. BACK: REASON TO LAUGH (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: REASON TO LAUGH (7), ARE WEASLEY (5), MAMMALS BLAZE (6), GOZO MAJOR (4) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R3 #6 OUR TINKA BELLE – 2 units (win) R4 #8 WEONA OUR RIGHTS – 1.5 units (each-way) R7 #2 BEAUTIFUL SUNRISE – 3 units (win) R8 #7 REASON TO LAUGH – 2 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 2,3,5,6,7,8,10/1,3,4,6,7/6,7,9/1,2,5,8 QUADDIE 2,5,8,9/3,7/2,4,6/4,5,6,7 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: LOUGLE (10) is yet to win this campaign, but strikes a very suitable assignment in the first race at Melton where he is a clear ratings topper at NR80. Now back in the care of Gerard Jamieson after a short stint with Stephen Clarke, the five-year-old heads here after a very good effort for second in last Friday’s Swan Hill Pacing Cup where he started second favourite behind The Final Dance. He raced off the fence in the chair for much of the event but still managed to fight on and only be beaten 7.6m. Hard to see him not going close. I’m a big fan of THUNDERFIRE (8), who needs to be forgiven for a plain effort last time when he was caught outside the leader. His prior form is very, very good with unsuitable trips and he just needs the right run in transit to figure. VIVID DREAM (9) is a talented pacer on the rise for Dean Braun who looked the winner in a race on Victoria Cup night before being grabbed late by the handy Hitch To His Star, while PLATINUM JIVE (1) draws for a lovely trip on the fence and started the campaign with an exceptional win from the rear at Cranbourne. BACK: LOUGLE (10) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: LOUGLE (10), THUNDERFIRE (8), VIVID DREAM (9), PLATINUM JIVE (1)

OVERVIEW: Free for all pacing contest where Andy Gath holds a strong hand with stablemates MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (3) and YAMBUKIAN (2), with preference given to the former who perhaps will be able to glide to the front over the short trip. Last time, he led and bolted in a very suitable race as a short-priced favourite, which followed a fourth placing in a heat of the SA Cup. He’s a good horse on his day, and from the front he’d be hard to catch. YAMBUKIAN (2) ran okay from back in the field on Victoria Cup night in what was his first race in well over a year. If he can get to the fence, he will be hard to beat as he’s a multiple winner at FFA level here at Melton. Trainer Scott Ewen returns to the sulky behind BULLETPROOF BOY (7) with the absence of James Herbertson, who tried an early move last weekend in a bid to find the front that proved unsuccessful. Despite being caught parked, the old boy ran well for third behind Ghost Of Time and he’s certainly a major hope despite the wide gate. NEW SHUFFLE (8) is an emerging pacer who had the race run to suit last time but couldn’t get past the airborne Fairplay. He has performed very well all campaign and is another that could win without surprising, as could FOX DAN (5) after his Vicbred Super Series triumph and brave second to Storms Collide in track record time at Swan Hill last Friday. Intriguing race! SELECTIONS: MY ULTIMATE BARNEY (3), YAMBUKIAN (2), BULLETPROOF BOY (7), NEW SHUFFLE (8)

OVERVIEW: Wide-open clash between the trotters over the sprint trip where CENTURION DREAM (2) narrowly gets the nod from gate two. She led and was run down by CHARLESTON AVENUE (7) two starts back at Cranbourne over the middle trip and then made a break late in a race at Maryborough on Sunday that a few of these contested. She did a great job to get back down and finish just 15.8m from the winner, who was CHARLESTON AVENUE (7) again. If she can find the fence, expect her to go close. The flying CHARLESTON AVENUE (7) can certainly win, but it does look harder over the 1720m trip from wide on the front line, TIMMY TURTLE (5) was able to power forward, lead and bolt in last time over this trip and will likely try for the same result, while FREIGHT SHAKER (10) made an early gallop and ran into late trouble last time, but won and placed twice before that in good races at Melton and Geelong. He’s a contender from wide on the back line. SELECTIONS: CENTURION DREAM (2), TIMMY TURTLE (5), CHARLESTON AVENUE (7), FREIGHT SHAKER (10)

OVERVIEW: BETTORLEFTALONE (6) was beaten as a short-priced favourite on debut for new trainer Alex Ashwood last time at Kilmore by stablemate REFUSAL (8) but looks well placed to turn the tables here. BETTORLEFTALONE (6) was caught parked in that assignment and was only grabbed late by a horse with the perfect run, with his prior Victorian form for trainer Jason Grimson being a narrow defeat at Geelong, a good fourth in a heat of the Victoria Derby and then a down-the-track finish in the Group 1 final. He looks the class runner in this 58-66 clash. WHERE IS WOODY (1) had a horror gate but hit the line nicely from last first-up for the Andy Gath stable at Melton last weekend and can improve sharply from gate one, SHAZZA LOVE (3) has been well beaten her past few but looks a chance of finding the early lead and can be a contender from the pegs, while MY MATE ACE (2) has won all three starts this campaign and is a pacer on the rise. BACK: BETTORLEFTALONE (6) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETTORLEFTALONE (6), WHERE IS WOODY (1), SHAZZA LOVE (3), MY MATE ACE (2)

OVERVIEW: ALDEBARAN SUE (7) has run a couple of really nice races leading into this assignment, including last weekend when she chased home the smart Keayang Kurki in the Matchmaker Mile at Maryborough to only be beaten 9.4m into fourth. Before that, she was held up at the rear of the field then charged late for third behind Majestic Tooth and presents here with a great chance in what is another race with plenty of contenders. They include KENNYS SON (9), who made it back-to-back victories when taking out the Greg Sugars Memorial at Maryborough on Sunday, TICTOK (4), who seems to be right in the zone at the moment and made up stacks of ground for third in another race at Maryborough, and EL TORNADO (2), who broke late on Sunday when well fancied in the race won by KENNYS SON (9). A return to prior form has him as a leading hope. BACK: ALDEBARAN SUE (7) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: ALDEBARAN SUE (7), KENNYS SON (9), TICTOK (4), EL TORNADO (2)

OVERVIEW: MY LITTLE BO (7) presents third-up into the campaign in a race for horses rated no higher than 80 who have not won any race with advertised stakemoney of $15,000 or more in the last six months. First-up, she attempted to lead but was held out and did well to close off again for fourth behind Jaccka Evan. Then last time, she found the top, handed to the very smart Seathestars and chased him home into second while cutting the margin to 2.3m. I fancy she might be a chance of finding the front here from out wide on the front line and think she’s the horse to beat. EARL OF PEMBROKE (5) won a good race from the tail of the field at Melton back in early October when beating home MIGHTY JOLT (4) and KOSIMO (2), MIGHTY JOLT (4) has been racing well of late and should have the speed to get to the fence early where he’d be a major contender, while IMA TERMINATOR (1) isn’t setting the world on fire by any means but draws to run well over the sprint trip. BACK: MY LITTLE BO (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: MY LITTLE BO (7), MIGHTY JOLT (4), EARL OF PEMBROKE (5), IMA TERMINATOR (1)

OVERVIEW: LOWRIDER (9) was a red-hot $1.06 favourite in a race five of these horses contested last weekend at Melton, but he blew his chances with an early break. Despite losing stacks of ground, he chased hard and did a good job to only be beaten 12.1m despite finishing last. His last mile of 1:55.14 was seconds quicker than his rivals and a faultless display should see him finding the winner’s stall on the back of some competitive efforts through the Vicbred and Victoria Derby series. OWEN THE SAINTS (3) ran well in that race last weekend when only beaten 1.5m, KING BALDWIN (7) dropped out badly last time (no abnormalities reported by vets) in The Graduate but looks a promising pacer for the Ashleigh Herbertson yard, while BULLETPROOF KID (6) led that LOWRIDER (9) race last Saturday and fell into third after only being grabbed in the shadows of the post. He’s been thereabouts of late and is a contender for the minor end of the prize, as is OOH AH LISTAH (1) who didn’t have much clear air in that aforementioned contest. SELECTIONS: LOWRIDER (9), OWEN THE SAINTS (3), KING BALDWIN (7), BULLETPROOF KID (6)

OVERVIEW: Boom three-year-old filly BETTOR BEACH (5) is on a path to The Eureka and looks set to continue her winning ways in the final event on the card. She heads into this assignment on the back of five-straight wins, including Group 1 glory in the Vicbred Super Series and Victoria Oaks finals. She has brilliant speed and it’s hard to see how they beat her. She’ll be short and likely too good. DEMBE (3) was chasing five-straight victories when a good fourth in The Graduate last weekend at Melton and is a very promising three-year-old pacer for Isabel Walsh, TED (1) did it tough but got the job done on Australian debut in an easier race than this at Bendigo on August 20 and draws for a nice trip, while Julie Douglas-trained stablemates OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (6) and CLYMENUS (7) are honest types who could certainly run into a place with the right trip. OVERVIEW:STORMS (7) is resuming since a debut third but he has appeared to be very sharp at the trials having remained undefeated in three attempts. He zipped home his last quarter in 27.4 seconds at his latest trial success so he is worth following. CRYPTO CROOK (2) commenced from the pole position, was headed off at the start and settled three back on the markers when a fast finishing second at Charlton on debut. She created a good impression first up and should prove hard to beat. ITS HYDROMATIC (1) gained a nice trail and tried hard over the latter stages when third in the same race at Charlton. He possesses early speed and is ideally drawn so he warrants respect. BANGBANG BOBBIE (3) was runner up behind the smart juvenile pacer Lambro Louella at Mount Gambier last outing. He has been runner up twice recently and should be competitive again. HALF AS TOUGH (6) produced a game performance when a fast finishing second at Hamilton then couldn’t work into the race from a poor draw at Charlton. He is worth another chance despite the poor draw. SELECTIONS: STORMS (7), CRYPTO CROOK (2),ITS HYDROMATIC (1), BANGBANG BOBBIE (3)

OVERVIEW:EMILY VINCENT (2) set up a very genuine tempo in the lead and battled on okay for fourth in a slick mile rate of 1.54.5 at Kilmore last outing. She has only been placed once in 20 starts for the season but her efforts since resuming have been encouraging and she is drawn to go well. WICKED MITZI (1) is a fast beginner and is drawn to suit her racing pattern. She was shuffled back on the markers after commencing from the inside of the second row and didn’t have much room in the straight when sixth at Shepparton last outing. WILD CARD (3) has been racing at Metropolitan level and will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment. He was a winner at Cranbourne on September 06 and is worth thought again. EL LAZZAR (5) is stepping up in class on his latest performances but he racing in career best form. He led throughout from the pole position and recorded a mile rate of 1.55.0 at Swan Hill last week so he can take the next step forward. SELECTIONS: EMILY VINCENT (2), WICKED MITZI (1), WILD CARD (3), EL LAZZAR (5)

OVERVIEW: LOUS MAMBO (5) settled four back on the markers, moved into the death seat at the 1100m and battled on strongly for third behind Ozzie Tart in the Tatlow Stakes last outing. This race is much easier and he should prove hard to beat again. SWIM SUIT (2) also competed in the Tatlow Stakes and battled at the end, finishing in seventh. His form prior was sound and he led throughout at a Terang victory on October 19 so he is worth another chance. SURETHING (3) began quickly but couldn’t get across to the markers and ended up restraining to find a position on the inside mid-race when a creditable first up second. She should be fitter from that performance and is worth thought. PHILS BOY (4) and XLENDI STAR (6) are both capable of showing up without surprising. BACK: LOUS MAMBO (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: LOUS MAMBO (5), SWIM SUIT (2), SURETHING (3), XLENDI STAR (6)

OVERVIEW: TALKNPLAY (5) is stepping up in class from his past three successes but he has been dominating his rivals and is capable of taking the next step forward. He worked to the front and recorded a slick mile rate of 1.55.5 last time out. YANKEE RAIN (7) has also been in winning form and overcame a tough run to score comfortably at Ballarat last week. She is likely to endure a wide trip from the poor draw but she is racing too well to dismiss. JAMES GARNER (3) drew on the inside of the second line, was shuffled to three back on the markers and worked home nicely late for third at Charlton. He should have benefited from that performance and is better drawn so he must be respected. VILLAGE VOICE (6) was caught behind tiring horses before working home well once finding a clear passage at her latest second. She is capable of running into a place again. SELECTIONS: TALKNPLAY (5), YANKEE RAIN (7), JAMES GARNER (3), VILLAGE VOICE (6)

OVERVIEW:BETTOR DOO (1) recorded victories at Shepparton and Melton prior to enduring a tough run and finishing in fourth behind the in-form pacer Talknplay at Swan Hill. He is ideally drawn for this assignment and is capable of returning to winning form. PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (2) is a fast beginner and is a good chance of trying to lead throughout. He burst across from a wide draw to find the lead at Charlton and was only run down over the latter stages at his latest second. ONYX (8) missed away, settled last on the markers and finished off nicely via an inside run when fourth (4m) at Ballarat last week. He is likely to gain an economical trip from his trailing draw and is worth an investment. BOND GIRL (7) is terribly drawn and hasn’t raced since July but she was racing well enough last preparation to be competitive against this field. BACK: BETTOR DOO (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETTOR DOO (1), PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (2), ONYX (8), BOND GIRL (7)

OVERVIEW:MUSCLE VALLEY (10) finished off strongly and ran a great race for second in the Victoria Derby. He was also runner up in the Need for Speed Prince Final and this is a massive drop back in class so he is clearly the horse to beat. HAPPY ESCAPE (5) was runner up twice behind the handy mare Keayang Minnesota before a Maryborough victory, where he set up a slow tempo in the lead. He is racing at his peak form and looms as one of the leading chances again. WHY NOW (11) faces the tough handicap of 40m but he was placed off the same mark at Hamilton last outing so he cannot be dismissed. WHISKEY DAWN (9) continues to race consistently from the standing start and is capable of filling a place. BACK: MUSCLE VALLEY (10) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MUSCLE VALLEY (10), HAPPY ESCAPE (5), WHY NOW (11), WHISKEY DAWN

OVERVIEW: AVANT GUARD (9) commenced from the handicap of 20m, settled sixth on the outside and came out three horses wide from the 500m when he got home best to score at Maryborough last outing. He commences from the front tape here and should be competitive again. I DREAM OF MILLIE (10) is racing in great form and will prove hard to beat if she can step away safely but she does have an ordinary standing start record. She used plenty of energy early, took cover and battled on well for second in the Matchmaker Mile during the Redwood Carnival. CHAMPAGNE CHARLEY (7) has returned from a spell in terrific form and looms as one of the leading chances again. He left a trailing position to move up without cover from the 1100m when third at Maryborough last outing. ROMANTIC NINA (3) made an error in the Maryborough Cup last outing and finished in sixth. She appears to be well placed from the front row and will take beating if she can deliver a fool proof display. SELECTIONS: AVANT GUARD (9), I DREAM OF MILLIE (10), CHAMPAGNE CHARLEY (7), ROMANTIC NINA (3)

OVERVIEW: ZENARIO (5) is a versatile pacer, which has been freshened since a close second behind Places You Don’t in a heat of the Australian Drivers Championship at Globe Derby, where he attempted to lead throughout. He recorded slick time at a Maryborough trial victory last week and should well. ROCKIN GEMMA (4) is racing in career best form having won four of her past five starts with her only miss being in a heat of the South Australian Cup. She broke the track record at Port Pirie three starts ago so she warrants respect. ROADMASTER (10) was placed in a heat of the South Australian Cup before drawing awkwardly and being in the second half of the field throughout in the Final. He is a speedy pacer and should be hitting the line strongly. WORDS (9) has been racing at Metropolitan level and she is likely to find this race to be a little easier. She was shuffled back on the markers and finished sixth (8m) in the Ladyship Cup last outing. TELEMACHUS (1) is ideally drawn and won the 2023 St Arnaud Cup at his only attempt on the track. SELECTIONS: ZENARIO (5), ROCKIN GEMMA (4), ROADMASTER (10), WORDS (9)

OVERVIEW: BLACK OPAL JACK (2) is a tough type, which should be getting fitter after his two starts back from a spell and will appreciate his best draw for a long time so a forward showing is expected. DELIGHTFUL CHARM (8) is resuming from a spell and hasn’t been to the trials but she was competitive at a much higher level when she was last in work. She has the perfect trailing draw so she cannot be dismissed. HUXHAM CHUBB (9) delivered a career best performance when she sustained a long run from last at the 800m to score at Hamilton. This race is no harder and she looms as a strong winning chance again. MISTER JIMARINGLE (7) pushed forward to race without cover and produced a strong performance when he scored at Kilmore last outing. He gets into this race nicely with a concession claim and is worth thought again. The stable mates IMAGINATION ORO (3) and YNOBE NOVA (4) are both fast beginners and have claims in an open race. SELECTIONS: BLACK OPAL JACK (2), DELIGHTFUL CHARM (8), HUXHAM CHUBB (9), MISTER JIMARINGLE (7)

OVERVIEW: BETA THAN LOVE (1) trailed the leader and used the sprint lane when second behind Bettor Doo at Melton last outing. He was narrowly beaten at his two starts prior and he strikes a very suitable assignment now. THE REGULATOR (8) finished off well when a close second behind Wichita Kansas at Ballarat last outing. He has the perfect trailing draw behind BETA THAN LOVE (1) and is one of the leading chances again. ARRAPS (5) possesses early speed and attempted to lead throughout when fourth behind Reason To Laugh at Kilmore last outing. He has been placed in three of his past five starts so he is worth a ticket each way. DULCIE MAUREEN (2) produced a career best performance when she was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off well at her latest second. She is nicely drawn and a repeat performance could see her filling a place again. BACK: BETA THAN LOVE (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BETA THAN LOVE (1), THE REGULATOR (8), ARRAPS (5), DULCIE MAUREEN (2)
